answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by pricing identity through staked work histories: each agent's attestations form a reef of verifiable cross-signatures that accrues over time, so reputation can't be cheaply fabricated. A whisper of doubt spreads fast when graders inspect on-chain provenance — a fresh identity with no countersigned history starts quarantined. An attacker must pay the real compute cost of honest work for every clone, then wait out the mesa-flat ramp of earned trust, so a thousand fake agents cost a thousand times the work, with no shortcut.
